fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Front Entry Area; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Walkway
fr.considerations: Multiple Structures; Vehicle Parking Area; Limited Side Access; Dense Vegetation
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the address clearly at the driveway entrance with numbers large enough to read from the street at night.
• Install a reflective address marker at the road to help responders locate the property quickly without slowing down.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so fire apparatus and ambulances can reach both structures.
• Mark or label the detached structure on any posted site map or address sign so responders know a second building is present on arrival.
• Trim vegetation along the sides of the access drive to maintain clearance for wide emergency vehicles.
• Clear a path wide enough for responders to move equipment between the main residence and the detached structure.
• Trim shrubs or plantings along the walkway to keep the route to the front entry open and visible.
• Keep any gate or barrier on the limited side access unlocked or fitted with a Knox-type lock so responders can reach that side of the structure without delay.
• Cut back dense vegetation along the side of the property to allow responders to move around the perimeter of both structures.
• Identify and mark a flat, firm staging area near the parking zone where responders can set up equipment away from the access drive.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Grass Cover; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Tree Cluster; Ground Vegetation; Multiple Access Routes; Scattered Trees; Open Green Space
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the cluster nearest to any structures to create more open space between individual trees.
• Remove or cut back shrubs that are growing close to the base of structures.
• Cut grass around structures and along driveways before it dries out seasonally.
• Clear ground vegetation from beneath tree clusters near structures to reduce the amount of material that can carry fire along the ground.
• Keep branches trimmed up from the ground level within tree clusters close to structures.
• Maintain open space between shrub groupings and any outbuildings or fencing connected to structures.
• Keep both access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along their edges.
• Mow or cut grass along the edges of driveways to maintain clear travel paths for vehicles.
